pr_title: Improve UX importing images and sprites
pr_body:
Introduce drag & drop operations to let the user drag images and files and drop them on the timeline to allow the user merge the content properly instead of always opening new files. 
Fix #131.

Supported features:
- Drag & drop files between layers, frames, or in a cel of the timeline:
  If the file is dropped on a cel and has only one image, then it will replace the existing cel's image. Otherwise it is appended as a new layer.
  If the file is dropped between layers, its cels/frames will be inserted after the currently selected frame.
  If the file is dropped between frames, the layer will be inserted after the currently selected layer. 
- Drag & drop images from other apps (i.e. from a browser) between layers, frames, or in a cel of the timeline:
  If the dropped element is an animation (like a gif or animated webp) only the first frame is imported.
  If the image is dropped on a cel, then it will replace the existing cel's image.
  If the image is dropped between layers, one cel/frame will be inserted after the currently selected frame.
  If the image is dropped between frames, the layer will be inserted after the currently selected layer. 
- Drag & drop images from other apps outside of the timeline: A new document with the image is created.

issue_context.title: Import image as a new layer
issue_context.body:
_From [davidcapello](https://code.google.com/u/davidcapello/) on July 09, 2012 17:41:23_

What do you need to do? Import an existent image as a layer. How would you like to do it? With an option in "Layer > Import File as Layer" or "File > Import as Layer".

_Original issue: http://code.google.com/p/aseprite/issues/detail?id=131_

Reported in several other places:
* https://community.aseprite.org/t/adding-images-as-layers/5500
* https://community.aseprite.org/t/importing-image-to-a-specific-layer-frame/6834
* https://community.aseprite.org/t/question-about-importing-pngs-for-animation/7937
comments:
_From [davidcapello](https://code.google.com/u/davidcapello/) on April 26, 2014 15:24:12_

Or "Import as Frame" to import several files as frames. (We should enable multiple selection in the file selector.)

Also when dragging multiple files into the tool it would be nice to have a dialog that asks whether to import as separate files, one multi-layer file or one multi-frame file (the last one could replace the pretty cool automatic recognition of consecutive numbers in file names that unfortunately does not work if there are gaps in the numbers)

I'd like to see this; I'm drawing sprites over renders of a 3D animation exported from Blender (a rough armature model to ensure the animations are consistent and perspective correct from each isometric angle) and I can't see a way of adding more frames from external files.  As per the ticket, there's no function to do it directly, but I don't seem to be able to copy cels between open documents either which might've been a workaround.  I can just make the new frames in a separate file for now and merge their exports.
Would be nice to have this as a command line flag, too.
I just bought aseprite and assumed this would be possible - not sure how I'm supposed to import my previous work into aseprite without something like this.
Hi @bitlather, do you mean importing your work from the trial version? Check this post: https://community.aseprite.org/t/demo-trial-version/26

No, I meant importing from GIFs that I created in my previous tool - pyxeledit. I had multiple layers, and I wanted to export them as separate animated gifs and re-import them.

However, I think I just figured it out - it looks like I can select multiple frames, copy, and then paste into a different file. It didn't seem to work the first time; I'm able to replicate the error.

1. Have two gifs with an equal number of frames and same width/height.
2. Click & drag one gif into aseprite to create a file. Save it as an ASE file. We'll call this tab "A".
3. Click & drag another gif into aseprite. This will create a new tab. We'll call this tab "B".
4. Click the left-most frame of the animation, scroll to the right, hold in shift, and click the right-most frame in the animation.
5. Press ctrl+c to copy.
6. Go to tab "A", create a new layer, and paste.
7. Only a few frames are pasted.

However, this worked:

8. Go back to tab "B", click on the left-most frame, hold down the mouse button, then drag to the right-most frame.
9. Press ctrl+c.
10. Return to tab "A".
11. You can now paste the frames.

Thanks for responding so quickly. I assumed there wasn't a solution based on the other comments in this thread, but I am able to do what I need to do - it's just the issue outlined above made it seem like you could not copy and paste multiple frames to a different aseprite file.

Oh yeah, to select multiple frames you can press-and-hold the mouse button and drag it to select a range of frames to copy and then pasting then in other file. Using Shift+click to select multiple frames (e.g. the first one and the last one) will not select the whole range of frames, it will select only the first frame and the last one (anyway there are plans to change the #1498). I'm glad to see that you've figured it out.

Got it. I assumed shift+click would select a range, and ctrl+click would select individual frames. 

Anyway, I'm really happy to be migrating my files over; I've heard such good things about aseprite and decided it was time to make the switch.

We must consider that multiple options are possible on file/s Drag and Drop action: 1. Open each individual image file/s as separate sprite/s 2. Open image file/s as layers in a new sprite 3. Open image file/s as frames in a new sprite 4. Add image file/s as new Layers in current sprite (in a desired frame) 5. Add image file/s as new Frames in current sprite (in a desired layer) It would be very convenient adopt the behavior according where the files are dropped. For example: - 'A' region and the remaining areas: there're three options: 1, 2 or 3, so we'll need a dialog. - 'B' region: 4 or 5, so we will need a dialog too. - 'C' region: only 4 is possible, the cels will be allocated on different layers in the frame where the files were dropped. - 'D' region: only 5 is possible, the cels will be allocated on different frames in the layer where the files were dropped. Or simply a dialog with the 5 options. What do you think @dacap?

Hi @Gasparoken, that's right! I had a similar idea, but never liked the dialog for all cases, and I never thought about a dialog only for ambiguous regions, I think it's a nice solution for certain cases (the dialog should have a "don't show again" or something like that). Other possibility I was thinking was a combination with #2324 

My original idea included the tabs area to drop the external file as a new document (even more I think tabs should be animated so the drop operation is visible/we have some feedback), or drop it between layers to drop it as new layers, or between frames to add it as animation (the same for the timeline, I always wanted to make the timeline animated to expand a little space to know where the new file will be placed, and the same thing for drag-and-drop operations in the timeline itself, but that is another story/feature).

This wasn't implemented yet because:

1. Lack of time :(
2. There are some combinations that need some extra thought, e.g.
    * what happen if the dropped file contains multiple layers and we drop it between frames? should we add all layers?
    * what happen if the dropped file contains multiple frames and we drop it between layers? should we add all new frames at the beginning? (or in the current frame position?)
    * should it depend on the kind of image/animation? (e.g. if it's an image, we should be able to drop the image as a cel)
    * should we able to drop the file in a frame/layer (i.e. not between frames/layers, but in the same frame/layer)?
3. There is some pending cross-platform work to do: [DropFiles](https://github.com/aseprite/laf/blob/62e66a74bbbeb6ab2867f73e310f521f590b6d29/os/event.h#L39) event doesn't contain the mouse position inside the `os::Display`. Anyway this could be calculate with [System:: mousePosition()](https://github.com/aseprite/laf/blob/80ec051ecf4b702d769d4b2483e1a34b52368bde/os/system.h#L202) (although it would be better to get the mouse position from original the operating system event/message).

Interesting! I thought this only for single images.

For animations..., I think as first version of this feature, an animation dropped in a sprite should be allocated in a particular layer as a Flatten Visible animation.

And going further, It would be a super feature if that flatten copy isn't a copy, but an instance of the original file....yes, this can be take some time 😄 (even idk the deep coding implications).

Perhaps, we should start with something simple/experimental (the old Experimental feature trick😄)

You're amazing @dacap !

Any progress on this?

I would really love to have that feature as it takes a lot of time to copy paste each layer of a new image you want to add to your "currently working on" Aseprite file.
@martincapello please if you take this one contact me about the design, the best way would be to be able to drag and drop in the timeline area, and this requires a lot of laf work

I want to start tackling this feature (now that we have the necessary blocks in laf) but I would need to know a few things first:
1. Is there any pending changes on the Timeline (I think once you told me that you had some work in progress, but I'm not quite sure if I'm recalling correctly) that you would like to push before I start with this?
2. About the design, should I just follow the guidelines of these comments and ask for any gap I find while coding?
https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/issues/131#issuecomment-999115229
https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/issues/131#issuecomment-999527644
3. Do you prefer that I edit this issue's description to put together the design? We can then iterate over it to refine it.
4. I was about to send this comment, but just recalled that the drag & drop support is still missing in laf for Linux...should I do this first instead?

> 1. Is there any pending changes on the Timeline

My work in #4409, I hope to merge it soon.

> 2\. should I just follow the guidelines of these comments and ask for any gap I find while coding?

Probably we can start with something simple as the initial impl:
1) if the file is dropped in the timeline: it could be added as new layers (if it's one image, in the current frame, if it's another .aseprite file, all layers as new layers/all frames from the position we are),
2) outside of the timeline: it could be opened as a new doc (current behavior).
